He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Louisville Cardinals men's basketball|Louisville Cardinals]]. ==Early life and high school career== King is the son of Lo and Vincent King Sr. When he was in sixth grade at the [[United Faith Christian Academy]], he received his first Division I scholarship offer from [[Charlotte 49ers men's basketball|Charlotte]]. Prior to his freshman year of high school, King moved to [[Akron, Ohio]] and he attended [[St. Vincent–St. Mary High School]]. He became the first freshman to start on the team since [[LeBron James]] and he led the Fighting Irish to the state final.{{cite news |last1=Parker |first1=Brandon |title=Once compared to LeBron James, Louisville basketball recruit VJ King is flourishing his own way at Paul VI |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/highschools/once-compared-to-lebron-james-louisville-basketball-recruit-vj-king-is-flourishing-his-own-way-at-paul-vi/2016/01/04/c7f97506-b2f6-11e5-a842-0feb51d1d124_story.html |access-date=January 21, 2020 |work=[[Washington Post]] |date=January 4, 2016}} As a sophomore, he averaged 17 points per game and was named to the 2013–14 Associated Press Division II All-Ohio First Team alongside teammate [[Jalen Hudson]].{{cite news |last1=Cassilo |first1=Dan |title=St. Vincent-St. Mary's VJ King and Jalen Hudson, Central Catholic's Tervell Beck headline All-Ohio Division II boys basketball teams |url=https://www.cleveland.com/highschoolsports/article/st-vincent-st-marys-vj-king-and-jalen-hudson-central-catholics-tervell-beck-headline-all-ohio-division-ii-boys-basketball-teams/ |access-date=January 21, 2020 |work=[[The Plain Dealer]] |date=March 17, 2014}} King transferred to [[Paul VI Catholic High School]] in [[Fairfax, Virginia]] prior to his junior year where he was coached by Glenn Farello. He averaged 18.7 points per game as a junior and earned All-Met honors. On the AAU Circuit, King competed for Team Takeover where he averaged 14.2 points and 5.2 rebounds per game in 2015.{{cite news |last1=Johnson |first1=Chris |title=Five-star swingman V.J. King, a natural scorer, commits to Louisville |url=https://www.si.com/college/2015/06/13/vj-king-commits-louisville-2016-class-five-star-rick-pitino-kentucky-uconn |access-date=January 21, 2020 |work=[[Sports Illustrated]] |date=June 12, 2015}} King scored 35 points in a high school game in December 2015. As a senior, King averaged 22.9 points, 9.6 rebounds, 2.5 assists and 2.1 steals per game. He led the Panthers to a 20–11 record and to the Virginia Independent Schools Athletic Association Division I state championship game. He was a First Team All-Washington Catholic Athletic Conference honoree and was selected as the [[USA Today]] Gatorade Virginia Basketball Player of the Year. King was named a [[McDonald's All-American Game|McDonald's All American]] in 2016 and was selected to the [[Jordan Brand Classic]].{{cite news |title=Virginia Boys Basketball POY: V.J. King |url=https://usatodayhss.com/2016/gatorade-virginia-boys-basketball-poy-v-j-king |access-date=January 21, 2020 |work=[[USA Today]] |date=March 17, 2016}} King was a five-star recruit ranked No. 27 in his class according to [[ESPN]], while [[Rivals.com|Rivals]] ranked him No. 11 in the class of 2016. On June 12, 2015, King committed to [[Louisville Cardinals men's basketball|Louisville]], spurning offers from [[Arizona Wildcats men's basketball|Arizona]], [[UConn Huskies men's basketball|UConn]] and [[Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball|Virginia]] among others. He cited his relationship with Louisville assistant coach Kenny Johnson, previously an assistant at Paul VI, as crucial in his decision. ==College career== On February 6, 2017, King scored a career-high 24 points on 8-of-14 shooting in a loss against Virginia.{{cite news |last1=Greer |first1=Jeff |title=UofL's King encouraged by performance at UVa |url=https://www.courier-journal.com/story/sports/college/louisville/2017/02/08/louisville-basketball-vj-king-encouraged-performance-virginia/97641528/ |access-date=January 21, 2020 |work=[[Louisville Courier-Journal]] |date=February 8, 2017}} As a freshman at Louisville, King averaged 5.5 points per game off the bench. He started every game as a sophomore and averaged 8.6 points and 3.3 rebounds per game, shooting 32 percent from three-point range.{{cite news |last1=Lerner |first1=Danielle |title=Louisville basketball 2018-19: Can veteran V.J. King reach his potential? |url=https://www.courier-journal.com/story/sports/college/louisville/2018/08/01/can-louisville-basketball-veteran-v-j-king-peak-2018-19/867028002/ |access-date=January 21, 2020 |work=[[Louisville Courier-Journal]] |date=August 1, 2018}} As a junior, he started five games and averaged 3.9 points and 3.0 rebounds per game. After the season, he announced he was leaving Louisville and entered the [[2019 NBA draft]].{{cite news |last1=Lerner |first1=Danielle |title=V.J. King will not return to Louisville next season, Chris Mack says |url=https://www.courier-journal.com/story/sports/college/louisville/2019/04/25/louisville-basketball-vj-king-wont-return-chris-mack-says/3572004002/ |access-date=January 21, 2020 |work=[[Louisville Courier-Journal]] |date=April 25, 2019}} ==Professional career== After going undrafted in the 2019 NBA draft, King signed with the [[New York Knicks]].{{cite news |last1=Lerner |first1=Danielle |title=Louisville's V.J. King signs NBA deal with the New York Knicks, report says |url=https://www.courier-journal.com/story/sports/college/louisville/2019/06/21/louisvilles-v-j-king-signs-deal-with-nba-new-york-knicks/1523398001/ |access-date=January 21, 2020 |work=[[Louisville Courier-Journal]] |date=June 21, 2019}} He was waived by the Knicks on October 19, 2019.{{cite news |last1=Hersch |first1=Corey |title=Knicks waive guard Lamar Peters, forwards VJ King and Kenny Wooten |url=https://www.sny.tv/knicks/news/knicks-waive-guard-lamar-peters-forwards-vj-king-and-kenny-wooten/311223220/ |access-date=January 21, 2020 |work=SNY |date=October 19, 2019}} King joined their G League affiliate, the [[Westchester Knicks]].{{cite news |last1=Weir |first1=Josh |title=NBA G League Preview: Westchester Knicks at Canton Charge |url=https://www.cantonrep.com/sports/20191217/nba-g-league-preview-westchester-knicks-at-canton-charge |access-date=January 21, 2020 |work=[[The Repository]] |date=December 17, 2019}} King played in 13 of the team's first 15 games then missed roughly a month due to a strained hamstring and knee soreness. He returned to Westchester on January 18, 2020, and on January 31 posted his season high 17 points against the [[Maine Red Claws]]. King averaged 4.7 points and 2.3 rebounds in his rookie season.{{cite web |last1=Priczak |first1=Chris |title=2019-20 Westchester Knicks Season Recap: V.J. King |url=https://www.ridiculousupside.com/2020/4/13/21215671/2019-20-westchester-knicks-season-recap-v-j-king-nba-gleague |website=Ridiculous Upside |publisher=[[SB Nation]] |access-date=May 9, 2020 |date=April 13, 2020}} He was waived on February 1, 2022.{{cite web |title=NBA G League Transactions |url=https://gleague.nba.com/transactions/ |website=NBA.com |access-date=February 2, 2022}} On August 10, 2022, he signed with the [[Bristol Flyers]] of the [[British Basketball League]].{{cite web |title=Flyers confirm signing of VJ King |url=https://www.britishbasketballleague.com/flyers-confirm-signing-of-vj-king/ |website=[[British Basketball League]] |access-date=September 29, 2023 |date=August 10, 2022}} King averaged 18.2 points, 6.6 rebounds and 2 assists per game, earning BBL Team of the Year honors.{{cite web |title=VJ King named in BBL Team of the Year |url=https://www.bristolflyers.co.uk/news/vj-king-named-in-bbl-team-of-the-year/ |website=Bristol Flyers |access-date=September 29, 2023 |date=May 9, 2023}} On June 30, 2023, he signed with [[Hamburg Towers]] of the [[Basketball Bundesliga]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.hamburgtowers.de/news/ein-king-wechselt-aus-dem-koenigreich-nach-hamburg/|title=Ein King wechselt aus dem Königreich nach Hamburg|last=|first=|date=June 30, 2023|website=hamburgtowers.de|publisher=Sportando|language=de|access-date=August 12, 2023}} On July 18, 2024, he signed with [[Victoria Libertas Pesaro]] of the Italian [[Lega Basket Serie A]] (LBA).{{Cite web|url=https://www.victorialibertas.it/la-carpegna-prosciutto-basket-pesaro-chiude-il-roster-2024-2025-col-botto-firmato-v-j-king/|title=La Carpegna 30, 2025, he signed with [[Bursaspor Basketbol]] of the [[Basketbol Süper Ligi]] (BSL).{{Cite tweet |user=BsBasketbol |number=1957750756909457596 |title=Hoş geldin Vincent King Jr.}} ==National team career== King competed in the [[2013 FIBA Under-16 World Championship]] representing the United States. He helped the team go 5–0, winning the title while averaging 8.2 points and 5.2 rebounds per game. King competed in the [[2014 FIBA Under-17 World Championship]] representing the United States. He helped the team go 7–0, winning the title while averaging 6.7 points and 2.9 rebounds per game.{{cite web |title=VJ King |url=https://www.usab.com/basketball/players/mens/k/king-vj.aspx
